risks.quote: Regularly assessing the performance and impact of A.I. tools on teaching, learning, and academic outcomes, and making necessary adjustments to improve effectiveness and mitigate potential biases.

responsibilities.quote: Humans oversight is essential. Humans must remain responsible for decisions informed or supported by AI.
Ensures that proposed AI technologies undergo the appropriate academic, ethical, and governance review before procurement or approval for use.
Refrain from using or adopting AI tools that process institutional or personal data without appropriate review and approval.
Use AI technologies—whether institutionally supported or externally adopted—in accordance with privacy, academic integrity, and ethical guidelines.
Ensuring institutionally adopted A.I. technologies comply with relevant privacy regulations and align with our commitments to transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy.
Collected, stored, or processed data must be used ethically and responsibly.
Report concerns or risks associated with AI tools to their supervisor, IT, or the relevant academic or administrative unit.
Providing training and support to faculty and staff on the appropriate selection, use, adoption, and integration of A.I. technologies.
This Artificial Intelligence (A.I.) Policy will be reviewed annually to ensure its alignment with the evolving needs of the institution, and advancements in AI technologies.
